messages:
jen: Customer reports streaming cut after ~65s, then client reconnects but receives 401 and stream never resumes. They attached a pcap and a short repro.
jen: Repro notes: client opens SSE -> runs ~60s -> silence -> client issues reconnect with Last-Event-ID but Authorization header is missing on the reconnect HTTP request. Customer says this started after we put Cloudflare in front of ALB.
jen: Minimal curl from their capture: 
```
curl -v -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?user=abc' \\n  # output shows initial stream ok, then on reconnect: 
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?user=abc&resume=1' \\n  # Request headers: no Authorization header present in reconnect in capture
```
jen: Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-901 :customer: escalation. Looking for quick triage steps. :pray:

sam: Thanks Jen. Can you paste the proxy/access logs for the reconnect request (nginx/ALB)? Need to verify if ALB re-originated the request or CF re-issued it.
sam: My hunch: ALB idle_timeout = 60s, Cloudflare origin keepalive shorter, so CF is closing and re-establishing to origin and might be dropping Authorization when it retries (worker or origin cache config). Also possible Cloudflare's retry code turns it into an anonymous request.

maria: Pasted a snippet from access logs: 
```
2026-03-16T14:02:12Z GET /v1/stream 200 0.3s src=1.2.3.4 cf-connecting-ip=5.6.7.8
2026-03-16T14:03:17Z GET /v1/stream 401 0.01s src=cloudflare-worker cf-req-id=abcd1234  # reconnect, no auth header
```
maria: We also see a 401 spike 14:02-14:06 (auth.rate 0.45 -> 0.9).
maria: Cloudflare config shows Origin Keepalive TTL = 30s and Max Idle Conns = 6. ALB default idle is 60s. When CF closes the origin TCP earlier than ALB expects, it can open a new connection and replay headers differently.

alex: Two quick remediations:
- short-term: patch the worker to preserve Authorization on retry/resume requests (we can add `request.headers.set('authorization', cfRequest.headers.get('authorization'))` in worker) and deploy to prod.
- medium-term: increase ALB idle_timeout to 120s OR set Cloudflare origin keepalive to >= ALB idle. Also consider enabling TCP keepalive on origin connections.

sam: Also ask the client engineers to re-send Authorization on reconnects. SSE reconnects are just new HTTP requests; some client libs drop auth on automatic reconnects if using browser fetch with credentials omitted. Not our first choice but low friction for customer-side fix.

jen: Added: customer says their client is a mobile SDK that doesn't attach auth on automatic reconnect after a network flit. So both sides contribute.

maria: I've opened an internal infra task to make our ingress tolerant: detect reconnects with Last-Event-ID and allow a short grace window to accept resume token in query param if Authorization missing (audit log required). WIll coordinate with security.

ops-bot: Incident INFR-901 created/linked. Pagerduty alert suppressed for now. Rollout note: we will patch CF worker on canary first.

support-bot: Quick patch pushed to edge worker to forward Authorization for resume requests (rollout id: rwd-edge/worker/2026-03-16/patch-3). Monitoring: auth 401 rate -> 0.12 in canary, will promote in 10m if stable. :rocket:

alex: Follow-ups: add test that simulates CF->ALB origin connection churn and ensures Authorization preserved on reconnect replay. And add a telemetry label for "sse_resume_no_auth" so we can alert earlier.

jen: Customer notified of workaround and we asked them to update SDK to re-attach auth. Keeping ticket open until prod rollout and 24h stability.

sam: Thanks everyone. Summary: root cause likely Cloudflare origin->ALB connection churn + worker/CF retry path dropping Authorization on resumed SSE requests. Remediations: worker patch (done), ALB/CF keepalive alignment (scheduled), client SDK update (customer).

jen: Closing loop once 24h green. :white_check_mark:
